## Setup and Libraries


```{r}
#| label: setup
#| message: false
#| warning: false

library(SpaFun)
library(data.table)
library(fda)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
```

## Data Loading

The input is a table with the column `r_value` and one column per slide with
its L-cross function (see the "Lcross pipeline" vignette). On the HPC it is
read from disk:

```{r}
#| label: hpc-load-data
#| eval: false

input_file <- "/projects/shared/TCGA_data/results/combined_Lcross.csv"

message("Reading data from: ", input_file)
dt <- fread(input_file)
message("Successfully loaded data with ", nrow(dt), " rows and ", ncol(dt), " columns.")
```

Here we build it from the 5 example crops in `tcga_crops`, so this vignette
runs anywhere. With only 5 curves the analysis below is a demonstration:
the full analysis uses all the TCGA slides.

```{r}
#| label: load-data

data(tcga_crops)
r_values <- seq(0, 150, length.out = 70)

set.seed(10)
subs <- downsample(tcga_crops, method = "uniform", n_target = 5000,
                   marks = c("neoplastic", "stromal"), by_marks = TRUE)
L_list <- lapply(subs, function(x) {
  spatstat.explore::Lcross(x, i = "neoplastic", j = "stromal",
                           r = r_values, correction = "border")$border
})
dt <- data.table(r_value = r_values, as.data.table(L_list))
dim(dt)
```

## Functional Data Smoothing

We apply `funSmooth()` to convert the raw data points into a continuous
functional data object (penalised B-splines, see `?funSmooth`). The
coordinates of the TCGA slides are pixels at 40x: with `to_micron = TRUE`
and `magnif = 40` the grid `r` and the L values (lengths) are converted to
microns, assuming 0.25 micron/pixel at 40x (`mpp_ref`; set `mpp` if the
scanner resolution is known).

```{r}
#| label: fda-smoothing

smoothed_Lfun <- funSmooth(dt, norder = 4, Lfdobj = 2, fun_type = "L",
                           centered = FALSE, to_micron = TRUE, magnif = 40)
smoothed_Lfun
```

## Functional Principal Component Analysis (fPCA)

We perform Functional PCA on the smoothed $L$-functions. The number of
harmonics cannot exceed the number of curves: we use 3 with the 5 example
curves (10 on the full TCGA data).

```{r}
#| label: fpca-analysis

# Run fPCA
n_harm <- min(10, ncol(dt) - 2)
fpca <- pca.fd(smoothed_Lfun$fd, nharm = n_harm, smoothed_Lfun$fdPar)

# Assign sample names (excluding the 'r_values' column) to the PCA scores
rownames(fpca$scores) <- colnames(dt)[-1]
```

## Unsupervised Clustering

We apply two clustering techniques to the scores of the first two
principal components. On the full data we look for 6 groups; with the 5
example curves we use 2.

### K-means & Hierarchical Clustering

```{r}
#| label: clustering

# Set seed for reproducibility
set.seed(123)

# number of groups: 6 on the full data, fewer with the example curves
k <- min(6, nrow(fpca$scores) - 3)

# K-means clustering
fpca_km <- kmeans(fpca$scores[, 1:2], centers = k)

# Hierarchical clustering (Ward's method)
fpca_hc <- hclust(dist(fpca$scores[, 1:2]), method = "ward.D2")
memb_hc <- cutree(fpca_hc, k = k)
```

### Cluster Distribution Comparison

Below are the distribution tables comparing the cluster assignments between both methods.

```{r}
#| label: cluster-tables

message("K-means cluster sizes:")
table(fpca_km$cluster)

message("Hierarchical clustering cluster sizes:")
table(memb_hc)
```

## Visualizations

### Smoothed L-functions Plot

We visualize the smoothed $L$-functions, color-coded by their K-means cluster assignments.

Function to plot the smoothed Lcross functions

```{r}
#| label: function-plot_smoothed_Lfun

utils::globalVariables(c("r", "L_value", "L_plot_value", "Slide", "cluster"))

#' plot_smoothed_Lfun Function to plot the smoothed Lcross object
#' 
#' @param smoothed_obj A `spafun_fd` object from [funSmooth()] (or a list with elements `r` and `fd`).
#' @param clusters_vec vector of cluster value for each sample, named after the samples
#' @param mark_i name of the mark value for which the Lcross function was calculated
#' @param mark_j name of the mark value for which the Lcross function was calculated
#' @param center_plot to choose if you want the plot centered (L-r ~ r) or not. If the curves were already centered in `funSmooth()` (`centered = TRUE`), they are not centered again.
#' @importFrom fda eval.fd
#' @importFrom tidyr pivot_longer
#' @importFrom dplyr mutate left_join
#' @importFrom ggplot2 ggplot geom_hline geom_line theme_minimal labs theme aes 
#' @importFrom utils globalVariables
#' @return A ggplot object
#' @export

plot_smoothed_Lfun <- function(smoothed_obj, clusters_vec, mark_i = "Mark 1", mark_j = "Mark 2", center_plot = TRUE) {
  
  # 1. Extract the distance vector (r)
  r_vec <- smoothed_obj$r
  
  # 2. Evaluate the functional data object (fd) to get smoothed values
  # This creates a matrix where rows are 'r' distances and columns are samples
  smooth_mat <- eval.fd(r_vec, smoothed_obj$fd)
  
  # 3. Convert the matrix to a data.frame and prepare for ggplot
  df_smooth <- as.data.frame(smooth_mat)
  df_smooth$r <- r_vec
  
  # Pivot to long format
  df_long <- pivot_longer(
    df_smooth,
    cols = -r,
    names_to = "Slide",
    values_to = "L_value"
  )
  
  # 4. Center the L-function (L(r) - r) if requested, using the flag stored
  # by funSmooth to avoid centering twice
  already_centered <- isTRUE(smoothed_obj$centered)
  if (center_plot && !already_centered) {
    df_long <- df_long |> mutate(L_plot_value = L_value - r)
  } else if (!center_plot && already_centered) {
    df_long <- df_long |> mutate(L_plot_value = L_value + r)
  } else {
    df_long <- df_long |> mutate(L_plot_value = L_value)
  }
  
  # 5. Prepare the cluster metadata from the named vector (memb_hc)
  cluster_df <- data.frame(
    Slide = names(clusters_vec),
    cluster = as.factor(clusters_vec)
  )
  
  # 6. Join the functional data with the cluster assignments
  df_final <- df_long |> 
    left_join(cluster_df, by = "Slide")
  
  # 7. Build the ggplot, with the unit of r if known
  unit_lab <- if (!is.null(smoothed_obj$unit)) paste0(" (", smoothed_obj$unit, ")") else ""
  p <- ggplot(df_final, aes(x = r, y = L_plot_value, group = Slide, color = cluster)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50") +
    geom_line(alpha = 0.7, linewidth = 0.6) + 
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(
      title = paste0("Smoothed L-cross Function: ", mark_i, " vs ", mark_j),
      subtitle = ifelse(center_plot, 
                        "Centered L-function (L(r) - r). Positive = Attraction, Negative = Repulsion", 
                        "L-function L(r)"),
      x = paste0("Radius r", unit_lab),
      y = paste0(ifelse(center_plot, "L(r) - r", "L(r)"), unit_lab),
      color = "Cluster"
    ) +
    theme(legend.position = "right")
  
  return(p)
}
```


```{r}
#| label: plot-l-functions
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 6

plot_smoothed_Lfun(
  smoothed_obj = smoothed_Lfun, 
  clusters_vec = fpca_km$cluster, 
  mark_i = "neoplastic",  
  mark_j = "stromal",
  center_plot = TRUE      # Subtracts 'r' (funSmooth was run with centered = FALSE)
)

```

### PC Scores Comparison

Finally, we project and compare the sample distributions in the reduced PCA space using both clustering results.

```{r}
#| label: plot-pc-scores
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 5

# Set up side-by-side plotting layout
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))

# K-means plot
plot(fpca$scores[, 1], fpca$scores[, 2], col = fpca_km$cluster, pch = 3, main = "K-means")
abline(v = 0, lty = "dashed", col = "grey")
abline(h = 0, lty = "dashed", col = "grey")

# Hierarchical clustering plot
plot(fpca$scores[, 1], fpca$scores[, 2], col = memb_hc, pch = 3, main = "Ward.D2")
abline(v = 0, lty = "dashed", col = "grey")
abline(h = 0, lty = "dashed", col = "grey")

# Reset layout
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```
